sections.heading: Sums as limits: the definite integral

questions.q: Explain how the definite integral $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$ is defined as a limit of Riemann sums, and write the limit expression using sigma notation.
questions.answer: $\int_a^b f(x)\,dx=\lim_{n\to\infty}\sum_{i=1}^{n}f(x_i^*)\Delta x$, where $\Delta x=\frac{b-a}{n}$ and $x_i^*$ is any sample point in the $i$-th subinterval — as $n\to\infty$ (subintervals shrink to zero width), all Riemann sum types (left, right, midpoint) converge to the same value, the exact signed area under $f$.

questions.q: Determine whether the Left Riemann Sum overestimates or underestimates $\int_0^4 x^2\,dx$, and explain why using the shape of the graph.
questions.answer: Since $f(x)=x^2$ is increasing on $[0,4]$, the left endpoint of each subinterval gives the smallest function value on that subinterval, so the Left Riemann Sum UNDERESTIMATES the true area (confirmed: $L_4=14 < \frac{64}{3}\approx21.33$).
